program_name: Urban and Political Geography is NOT a standalone degree. It is one of three second-year PATHWAYS ('ambiti formativi' / specialisation tracks) inside the master's degree whose official name on the University of Turin application portal is 'Geography and Territorial Sciences' (apply.unito.it course id 336). The Italian legal name of the parent degree is 'Corso di Laurea Magistrale Interateneo in Geografia e Scienze Territoriali', UNITO internal degree-programme code [0901M22], unito.it degree id 90932. The three second-year pathways are: (1) Geomorphological Hazards and Climate Change / 'Rischi geomorfologici e cambiamento climatico' (Italian only), (2) Landscape and Heritage Protection and Enhancement / 'Tutela e valorizzazione del paesaggio e del patrimonio' (Italian only), and (3) URBAN AND POLITICAL GEOGRAPHY (entirely in English). A cross-cutting GEO-DATA SCIENCE skill set (geomatics, GIS, remote sensing, photogrammetry/drones, programming, databases, big data, AI) can be added within any of the three pathways. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FACT: the degree is INTER-UNIVERSITY - the diploma is awarded jointly by the Universita degli Studi di Torino (UNITO) and the Politecnico di Torino. It is administered by the Interuniversity Department of Regional and Urban Studies and Planning (Dipartimento Interateneo di Scienze, Progetto e Politiche del Territorio, DIST), with the Department of Earth Sciences (Scienze della Terra) and the Department of Historical Studies (Studi Storici) as co-referring departments, under the School of Science of Nature (Scuola di Scienze della Natura). Director of the Master / pathway tutor: Prof. Michele Lancione (michele.lancione@unito.it).
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale; 'POSTGRADUATE DEGREE' on apply.unito.it). Nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS. Mode: full-time, with the note 'For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly.' Structurally it is an INTERUNIVERSITY (interateneo) degree jointly awarded by UNITO and Politecnico di Torino - i.e. case (3) of the teaching_language typology overlaps here with case (2), because the joint degree is Italian-named and only one of its three tracks is English.
teaching_language: Case 2 + Case 3 combined: an ENGLISH-TAUGHT PATHWAY inside an Italian-named INTERUNIVERSITY degree. Unlike Smart Agriculture or Viticultural and Enological Sciences (where only part of the credits are available in English), the Urban and Political Geography pathway is officially described as covering the FULL two years in English. apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' for course 336 (JSON feed field: "language": "en", i.e. English only, NOT the 'en~it' combined value used for the partial-English UNITO pathways). The official programme brochure states verbatim: 'Students choosing this pathway can study in English for the entire duration of the Master. In the first year, they are offered modules in human and physical geography, while in the second they will be able to choose courses focused on urban and political geography.' MECHANISM: in the first year the study plan is built as a series of 'one course to choose among' slots, each offering an Italian-language option and an English-language option; an English-track student picks the English option in each slot. Brochure course map for the English pathway - FIRST YEAR: Geography, theory and practice; Urban and regional development; Geomorphology and soil conservation; Urban studies; History, spaces and theories of capitalism; Remote sensing; Advanced (or basic) GIS; Lab: Methods for Geographical Research. SECOND YEAR: Urban political geography; Critical migration studies; Housing, property and struggles; Southern urbanism; Racialised and gendered cities; Lab: Geopolitics: Israeli-Palestinian conflict; Vocational training; Master's Degree Thesis. The Italian-language microsite (updated 03/12/2025) confirms 'URBAN AND POLITICAL GEOGRAPHY ... Gli insegnamenti di questa specializzazione sono offerti in lingua inglese', and describes the other two tracks as 'offerti prevalentemente in italiano' (predominantly in Italian). NO Italian-language requirement is imposed for admission. [uncertain - the pathway label 'Urban and Political Geography' is a curriculum/track name, not a separately accredited degree; the diploma awarded is the Italian LM-80 'Laurea Magistrale in Geografia e Scienze Territoriali'. Also uncertain: the year-by-year availability of an English option in EVERY first-year slot for 2026/27. The English microsite study-plan page (www.geography.unito.it .../View?doc=study_plan.html, the URL supplied in the research brief) is STALE - it is labelled 'coorte 2021' and stamped 'Last update: 19/05/2021', predates the current three-pathway structure entirely, and must not be treated as the current plan; the Italian piano_studi.html page is also stale (24/10/2022). The current per-course language assignment for a.y. 2026/27 should be checked in the live 'Insegnamenti' / course catalogue, which could not be fetched because *.unito.it refuses automated requests.]
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. apply.unito.it: 'Study location: Italy, Turin'; the Italian microsite sidebar states 'Sede didattica: Torino' and the English one 'Teaching seat: Turin'. Teaching is delivered in the city centre: the brochure states 'Students will attend lecture in our Departments, near the Valentino's Park in the city centre of Turin' - i.e. the DIST premises around the Castello del Valentino / Valentino Park area, shared between UNITO and Politecnico di Torino because the degree is interuniversity. UNITO's legal/administrative seat is Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino. No branch or satellite campus; no Grugliasco/Cuneo/Savigliano component.
degree_class: LM-80 - Scienze geografiche (Geographical Sciences), Italian second-cycle degree class. The Italian microsite title reads verbatim 'Corso di Laurea Magistrale Interateneo in Geografia e Scienze Territoriali (LM-80)'. UNITO internal degree-programme code: [0901M22]. unito.it / course-catalogue degree id: 90932. apply.unito.it course id: 336; apply.unito.it type code 'MA' / 'POSTGRADUATE DEGREE'. 120 ECTS over 2 years.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (Italian: 'corso senza numero chiuso' / accesso libero) - no numerus clausus, no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT, no ranked national selection. Both the Italian and English microsite sidebars state this explicitly ('Requisiti di accesso: corso senza numero chiuso' / 'Entry requirements: course without restricted number of places'). Operational proof: the course appears in the 'Fourth admission call for OPEN ACCESS postgraduate degree programs only' (25 August - 8 September 2026) on apply.unito.it, a window reserved to open-access postgraduate degrees. HOWEVER, open access here does NOT mean automatic admission. Admission is a two-stage departmental procedure ('ammissione preliminare'), described on the programme's own site: (A) a Commission verifies possession of the CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (requisiti curriculari); if satisfied, the candidate is admitted to (B) an ORAL INTERVIEW verifying 'adeguata preparazione personale' in the two core geographical disciplines. Candidates whose prior geography exams average 24/30 or higher may be exempted wholly or partly from the interview by decision of the Commission. Only after this preliminary admission does the candidate proceed to the actual enrolment ('iscrizione vera e propria') under University-wide administrative rules. NON-EU QUOTA: apply.unito.it 'Territory requirements' states 'This degree program has 75 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' (Note: unlike Smart Agriculture, the apply.unito.it text does NOT add a 'shared among all the curricula' sentence here, but since Urban and Political Geography has no separate degree code the 75 places must in practice cover the whole LM-80 degree including the two Italian-language pathways.) International applicants (holders of a foreign qualification) apply through the Apply@UniTo / DreamApply portal within one of the University's fixed admission calls; visa applicants must additionally complete Universitaly pre-enrolment.

entry_exam_or_test: No standardised entrance exam (no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT, no written admission test). Instead there is a MANDATORY ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW ('colloquio di verifica dell'adeguata preparazione personale'), preceded by a documentary curricular check. The brochure states plainly: 'Applications are evaluated by our academics, and an on-line oral colloquium is required.' - so the interview is held ONLINE, which matters for overseas applicants. PROCEDURE: (1) the candidate submits the online preliminary-admission form attaching the degree certificate with the full list of exams taken, showing SSD (Italian scientific-disciplinary sector), CFU/ECTS and grades, plus any other useful documents (single-exam certificates, English language certificates); self-certification (autocertificazione) is accepted; final-year bachelor students ('laureandi') may also apply provided they expect to graduate in time. (2) A dedicated Commission verifies the curricular requirements and, if met, admits the candidate to the interview, telling them the specific study programme to prepare. (3) The interview tests adequate knowledge of the two core disciplines: PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOMORPHOLOGY (GEOS-03/A, ex GEO/04) and HUMAN GEOGRAPHY (GEOG-01/A or GEOG-01/B, ex M-GGR/01 or M-GGR/02). Published syllabus for the interview - Physical geography/geomorphology: elements of cartography (map scale, reference systems and projections, map types); the solar system, size and shape of the Earth, the geographic grid, Earth's movements, the seasons; the atmosphere, insolation and temperature, pressure and winds, humidity and disturbances; climate classification and distribution; the hydrosphere (hydrological cycle, oceans, ice, surface and groundwater). Human geography: elements of cartography; key geographical concepts (environment, space, place, region, territory, landscape, scale, globalisation); population geography; development geography; urban geography (cities and urbanisation processes, urban functions, networks and hierarchies); location and spatial organisation of economic activities; transport and communication flows and networks; political geography (the state, international institutions, the intra-state level). Recommended texts are published (McKnight & Hess, 'Geografia Fisica'; Strahler; Haggett, 'Geografia'; Dematteis et al.). EXEMPTION: 'Gli studenti potranno essere esentati in tutto o in parte dal colloquio ... qualora nel loro curriculum pregresso risultino aver conseguito gli esami di Geografia (GEO/04, M-GGR/01 e M-GGR/02) riportando una valutazione media ponderata uguale o superiore a 24/30' - a weighted average of 24/30 or above in prior geography exams can exempt the candidate wholly or partly, at the Commission's discretion. Even directly-admitted candidates must formally register for one interview date (via MyUniTo > Iscrizioni > Test di valutazione) without attending, so that the office can compile the list of admitted candidates. GAP-FILLING: candidates missing some curricular CFU may enrol in single university courses ('singoli insegnamenti') and pass the corresponding assessment before the enrolment deadline. [uncertain - the 2026/27 interview dates and the interview registration window were still marked 'in via di definizione' (to be defined) on the microsite snapshot stamped 23/03/2026; for a.y. 2025/26 the published dates were 17 June, 10 July, 22 September, 17 October, 5 December 2025 and 12 January 2026, with registration open 23 May 2025 - 22 December 2025, which gives a realistic idea of the rhythm but is NOT the 2026/27 calendar. Also uncertain whether the interview is conducted in English for English-pathway applicants - the brochure's 'on-line oral colloquium' wording implies yes for international candidates, but no official page states the interview language.]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION. A first-cycle degree (bachelor's) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable. apply.unito.it: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education. You will also need to meet specific admission requirements and demonstrate a suitable academic preparation and a solid background.'

SUBJECT AREA OF THE BACHELOR'S - ROUTE 1 (degree class). apply.unito.it and the brochure state: 'To register for the Master's Program in Geography and Territorial Sciences, candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree in the domain of Geography, Territorial Sciences, Humanities, Natural Sciences, Economics, Political Sciences.' The English microsite expands this to: 'Geography; Architecture; Urban Planning; Urban Design; Geological Sciences; Cultural Heritage; History; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Agricultural and Forestry Sciences; Environmental and Nature Sciences; Economics; Political Science; International Relations; International Development and Cooperation.' The Italian regulation lists the exact Italian DM 270/2004 classes accepted: TERRITORIAL SCIENCES - L-6 Geografia, L-17 Scienze dell'architettura, L-21 Scienze della pianificazione territoriale, urbanistica, paesaggistica e ambientale, L-34 Scienze geologiche; HUMANITIES - L-1 Beni culturali, L-42 Storia; ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES - L-7 Ingegneria civile e ambientale, L-25 Scienze e tecnologie agrarie e forestali, L-32 Scienze e tecnologie per l'ambiente e la natura; ECONOMIC-POLITICAL SCIENCES - L-33 Scienze economiche, L-36 Scienze politiche e delle relazioni internazionali, L-37 Scienze sociali per la cooperazione, lo sviluppo e la pace. Old-ordinamento, specialistica and magistrale degrees in equivalent disciplines are also considered (ex DM 509 classes L30, L7, L16, L4, L13, L38, L20, L27, L8, L28, L15, L35), assessed by the Commission against the ministerial equivalence tables.

SUBJECT AREA - ROUTE 2 (credit-based alternative, the practical route for most foreign applicants). Candidates holding a degree in a class NOT listed above can still be admitted to the interview if their university career includes basic exams of at least: 6 CFU/ECTS in PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY AND GEOMORPHOLOGY (GEOS-03/A, ex GEO/04) AND 6 CFU/ECTS in HUMAN GEOGRAPHY (GEOG-01/A or GEOG-01/B, ex M-GGR/01 or M-GGR/02). apply.unito.it phrases the same rule as: 'Alternatively, candidates must have taken at least 6 ECTS credits in Physical Geography or Geomorphology and 6 ECTS in Geography or Economic-Political Geography.' If a candidate lacks some or all of these credits, they may enrol in single university courses (singoli insegnamenti) and pass the corresponding assessment before the enrolment deadline for the master's.

GPA / MARK THRESHOLD. There is NO published minimum GPA or minimum degree mark for admission. The only numeric threshold in the rules is an EXEMPTION rule working in the applicant's favour: a weighted average of 24/30 or above in prior geography exams (GEO/04, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02) can exempt the candidate, wholly or partly, from the personal-preparation interview at the Commission's discretion.

PLACES AND NON-EU QUOTA. The degree is open access with no overall cap on Italian/EU places ('corso senza numero chiuso'). For non-EU applicants residing abroad there IS a quota: apply.unito.it 'Territory requirements': 'This degree program has 75 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.'

DOCUMENT LANGUAGES. 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'

SCHOLARSHIPS (relevant because they are tied to the January deadline). The brochure advertises 'merit-base or income-base full-stipend scholarships'. At University level, 'Talents 4 UniTO' for a.y. 2026-2027 awarded '40 two-year scholarships to International Students who are enrolling for the first time in an English-taught postgraduate degree program without a restricted number of places' - this course qualifies on both counts (English-taught, open access). That call is now closed for 2026/27 and its ranking list has been published.

[uncertain - how a non-Italian transcript is mapped onto the Italian SSD codes GEOS-03/A and GEOG-01/A-B is decided case by case by the departmental Commission, and no published conversion table or pre-assessment form was found. It is also not stated anywhere whether the 75 non-EU places are formally shared with the two Italian-language pathways (they almost certainly are, since the pathways share one degree code), nor how many non-EU places have historically gone to the Urban and Political Geography track. The list of accepted Italian bachelor classes comes from the microsite page stamped 23/03/2026, retrieved via the Internet Archive because *.unito.it refuses direct fetches.]
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - the only language formally required; NO Italian requirement for admission.

APPLY@UNITO (the operative, most specific rule, from the apply.unito.it course record updated 2026-06-23): 'Applicants must hold an international certification (see below for list of accepted certifications and minimum scores requirements), certifying at least a CEFR B2 level of English language proficiency, OR must have taken at least one English language exam in their University curriculum.' Accepted certifications and minimum scores, verbatim: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate of English (FCE) - minimum score 173 (B); PTE Academic - minimum score 65; IELTS - minimum score 5.5 out of 9, with no partial score below 5.5; TOEFL iBT - minimum score 69 out of 120, no partial score below 17; Trinity College ISE II.

NOTE THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE: a certificate is NOT strictly mandatory - having passed at least one English-language exam within the bachelor's curriculum satisfies the requirement. The Italian regulation states the same: 'E altresi richiesta un'adeguata conoscenza della lingua inglese, sia in forma scritta sia in forma orale. Tale requisito e considerato soddisfatto se lo studente ha sostenuto nel proprio curriculum universitario almeno un esame di lingua inglese o possiede un certificato di conoscenza della lingua inglese di livello pari almeno al B2 del Quadro Comune Europeo, rilasciato da un ente accreditato.' The English microsite repeats it: 'An adequate knowledge of the English language is also required (evidenced by at least a university exam in English or a certificate of English language proficiency issued by a certified institution, at least to B2 level of the Common European Framework).' The brochure simply says 'Knowledge of the English language is also required.'

Note that the IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 69 thresholds published here are LOW by the standards of English-taught Italian master's programmes and sit at the B1/B2 boundary on most conversion tables, even though the University labels them as B2 evidence.

ITALIAN - NOT REQUIRED. Because the Urban and Political Geography pathway is delivered entirely in English, no Italian-language requirement appears anywhere in the admission rules for this degree: apply.unito.it's 'Language requirements' block for course 336 lists ENGLISH ONLY (contrast Smart Agriculture, where the block lists 'English / Italian'). The CLIQ Italian B2 certificate obligation does NOT apply: it is scoped to 'undergraduate or 5-6-year postgraduate degree programs with free admission taught in Italian', and this is a 2-year Italian-taught-in-part laurea magistrale whose English pathway is the one at issue. Italian would nonetheless be practically useful for daily life and for accessing the two Italian-language pathways, the Italian-language optional courses, and Italian-language internships.

[uncertain - it is not stated whether the online admission interview itself is conducted in English for candidates declaring the Urban and Political Geography pathway; nor whether an applicant whose bachelor's was taught entirely in English is exempt from producing any English evidence at all (this is standard practice at UNITO but is not written on the course record). Applicants should confirm with the Director, Prof. Michele Lancione (michele.lancione@unito.it), or the student office (rossana.petean@unito.it).]
required_documents:
TWO PARALLEL CHANNELS - which one applies depends on where your qualification was issued.

A) APPLY@UNITO / DreamApply (apply.unito.it) - for holders of a FOREIGN qualification. Course-specific items from the apply.unito.it course 336 record: (1) the first-cycle/bachelor's degree certificate plus a full transcript of exams taken, sufficient to prove either that the degree falls in one of the accepted domains (Geography, Territorial Sciences, Humanities, Natural Sciences, Economics, Political Sciences) or that at least 6 ECTS in Physical Geography/Geomorphology and 6 ECTS in Geography/Economic-Political Geography were passed; (2) evidence of English at CEFR B2 - either an accepted certificate (CPE / CAE / FCE 173(B) / PTE Academic 65 / IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 69 with no section below 17 / Trinity ISE II) or proof of an English-language exam in the university curriculum; (3) A MOTIVATION LETTER - listed explicitly under 'Other requirements' for this course ('A motivation letter must be added to your application') and also mandatory University-wide for all postgraduate applicants, in English or Italian.

General Apply@UniTo requirements for ALL postgraduate applicants: the documentation required for your specific foreign education system (secondary and university qualifications); the motivation letter; 'additional documents required by some specific postgraduate degree programmes (please refer to "Entry qualification", "Language requirements" and "Other requirements" in the degree program description), such as: minimum credit requirements and English language certifications'; optionally the degree-programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED here, because the Commission has to map your courses onto the Italian SSD codes; and payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (same amount whether you select one or two degree programmes).

Language of documents: 'All documents uploaded in your online application are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish. If your documents are issued in a different language, an official translation in one of the above-mentioned languages is also required.' After submission: 'we might require you to upload further documents (declaration of value, statement of verification, statement of comparability issued by CIMEA, etc.)', and 'during the enrolment step, the International Students Office might request further documentation'.

B) DEPARTMENTAL PRELIMINARY-ADMISSION FORM ('DOMANDA DI AMMISSIONE PRELIMINARE', online form on the programme microsite) - the route for Italian-qualification holders, and the mechanism by which the Commission assesses everyone. Required attachments, verbatim: 'il certificato di laurea con l'elenco degli esami sostenuti (con indicazione del Settore Scientifico-Disciplinare-SSD, dei Crediti Formativi Universitari-CFU e del voto conseguito) ed eventuali ulteriori documenti utili (attestati riguardanti esami singoli, certificati del livello conoscenza della lingua inglese, ...)'. Self-certification (autocertificazione) is accepted in place of official certificates. Final-year bachelor students may submit with just the transcript of exams passed so far. After the curricular check, registration for the interview is done through MyUniTo > Iscrizioni > Test di valutazione, which requires prior registration on the University portal.

C) VISA APPLICANTS (non-EU residing abroad) additionally complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment by 15 July 2026, indicating one degree programme only and the Italian Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested, then follow that mission's own visa document list.

[uncertain - no official page states whether reference letters, a CV, or a writing sample are expected for the Urban and Political Geography pathway specifically; only the motivation letter is named. It is also unclear whether a foreign-qualification applicant must complete BOTH the Apply@UniTo application and the departmental preliminary-admission form, or whether the Apply@UniTo submission is routed to the Commission automatically - the two procedures are documented on separate sites that do not cross-reference each other. Confirm with internationalstudents@unito.it and rossana.petean@unito.it.]

uncertainty_notes:
1) PATHWAY, NOT A SEPARATE DEGREE - THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT. 'Urban and Political Geography' has no independent degree code, no independent admission call, no independent quota and no independent diploma. It is one of three second-year pathways inside the interuniversity master's degree 'Geografia e Scienze Territoriali' / 'Geography and Territorial Sciences' [0901M22], class LM-80. The diploma awarded is the LM-80 Laurea Magistrale in Geografia e Scienze Territoriali, jointly by UNITO and Politecnico di Torino. Applicants apply to, and are admitted to, the parent degree; the pathway is chosen in the second year through optional and free-credit choices. Aggregator sites and even the programme's own promotional video ('Geography and Territorial Sciences (con Urban and Political Geography)') present it as a distinct master's, which overstates its independence.

2) BUT UNLIKE SMART AGRICULTURE, THE ENGLISH COVERAGE IS FULL, NOT PARTIAL. This is the key difference from the other UNITO partial-English pathways in this dataset. apply.unito.it records the study language for course 336 as plain 'English' (JSON "language": "en"), not the 'combined English/Italian' ('en~it') value used for Smart Agriculture and the other partial pathways, and the official brochure states that a student on this pathway 'can study in English for the entire duration of the Master'. The mechanism is that the first year is built from paired Italian/English course options and the English-track student takes the English option in each slot. Practical consequence: NO Italian is required to complete the degree on this pathway, and no Italian requirement appears in the admission rules.

3) INTERUNIVERSITY DEGREE - UNITO + POLITECNICO DI TORINO. The degree is awarded jointly by the two universities and is run by the shared DIST department (Dipartimento Interateneo di Scienze, Progetto e Politiche del Territorio). This research was scoped to unito.it sources only, so polito.it pages were deliberately NOT consulted; if the Politecnico publishes its own version of the admission rules, fee schedule or study plan for this degree, it was not checked. Prospective students should be told the diploma carries both universities' names, and that some teaching and facilities sit on the Politecnico side (Castello del Valentino area).

4) THE ENGLISH MICROSITE IS BADLY OUT OF DATE - INCLUDING THE URL SUPPLIED IN THE BRIEF. www.geography.unito.it/do/home.pl/View?doc=study_plan.html is stamped 'Last update: 19/05/2021' and labelled 'coorte 2021'; it does not mention Urban and Political Geography at all and lists a five-area second-year structure that has since been replaced by three pathways. why_study_with_us.html (19/05/2021) and admission_requirements.html / how_to_apply.html (October 2022) are likewise stale. The Italian piano_studi.html is stamped 24/10/2022. The CURRENT sources, in order of reliability, are: apply.unito.it course 336 (updated 23 June 2026, fetched live), the English brochure PDF (references the 2026/2027 application windows), the Italian presentazione.html (03/12/2025) and the Italian come_iscriversi.html (23/03/2026).

5) TWO PARALLEL, NON-CROSS-REFERENCED ADMISSION PROCEDURES. Apply@UniTo (for foreign-qualification holders, with fixed call windows and a EUR 60 fee) and the departmental 'DOMANDA DI AMMISSIONE PRELIMINARE' (open 10 March - 22 December 2026 for a.y. 2026/27, with the SSD/CFU transcript and the interview registration through MyUniTo) are documented on separate sites that never reference each other. It is NOT clear from official sources whether an international applicant must complete both, or whether the Apply@UniTo file is forwarded to the departmental Commission automatically. This should be confirmed with internationalstudents@unito.it before applying.

6) 2026/27 INTERVIEW DATES WERE NOT PUBLISHED. The microsite snapshot of 23 March 2026 still reads 'Le iscrizioni al colloquio di ammissione ... sono in via di definizione. Le date dei colloqui sono in via di definizione.' The 2025/26 cycle had six interview dates (17 June, 10 July, 22 September, 17 October, 5 December 2025, 12 January 2026) with registration open 23 May - 22 December 2025; that is a guide, not the current calendar. The same page also still carries an unfinished line for the previous year ('Per l'a.a. 2025/2026 l'iscrizione e da completare entro data da definirsi'), which indicates the page is maintained irregularly.

7) NON-EU APPLICANTS HAVE ONLY ONE WINDOW, AND IT HAS ALREADY CLOSED FOR 2026/27. The single 2026/27 window open to non-EU citizens residing abroad closed on 29 January 2026. The August-September 2026 window is expressly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy. As of 1 September 2026 a non-EU applicant abroad must target the 2027/28 first call (expected late November 2026 - late January 2027, not yet published). The same January deadline is the one tied to the merit-based scholarships, so it is doubly important.

8) THE 75 NON-EU PLACES ARE ALMOST CERTAINLY SHARED ACROSS ALL THREE PATHWAYS. apply.unito.it states '75 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad' without the 'shared among all the curricula' clarification it adds for some other UNITO degrees, but since the three pathways share a single degree code and a single application route, the quota must apply to the degree as a whole. No published data shows how many places have historically gone to the Urban and Political Geography track.

9) 'OPEN ACCESS' IS MISLEADING WITHOUT CONTEXT. The degree is legally 'corso senza numero chiuso', but admission still requires (a) a Commission check of curricular requirements and (b) an online oral interview on physical geography/geomorphology and human geography, with a published syllabus and recommended textbooks. Only candidates with a weighted average of 24/30 or better in prior geography exams may be exempted, and even they must formally register for an interview slot.

10) THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT IS THE REAL FILTER FOR CAREER-CHANGERS. Applicants whose bachelor's is not in one of the listed classes must show 6 ECTS in physical geography/geomorphology AND 6 ECTS in human geography. A candidate from, say, sociology, urban studies abroad, or anthropology may well fail this even though the pathway's subject matter (migration, housing, urban political geography) would suit them. How a foreign transcript is mapped onto the Italian SSD codes GEOS-03/A and GEOG-01/A-B is decided case by case by the Commission and no conversion table is published; the 'singoli insegnamenti' route exists to fill gaps but requires being in Italy or enrolled remotely before the master's enrolment deadline.

11) THE ENGLISH THRESHOLDS ARE UNUSUALLY LOW, AND A CERTIFICATE MAY NOT BE NEEDED AT ALL. IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.5) and TOEFL iBT 69 (no section below 17) are at the B1/B2 boundary on most conversion tables, yet UNITO presents them as CEFR B2 evidence. Moreover, both the Italian and English rules accept 'at least one English language exam in your University curriculum' as an alternative to any certificate. It is not documented whether a degree taught entirely in English counts, nor whether the admission interview itself is held in English for this pathway.

12) MINOR INCONSISTENCY IN THE PUBLISHED PATHWAY TUTOR. apply.unito.it (June 2026) names 'Tutor: Prof. Michele LANCIONE' for Urban and Political Geography and the brochure names him 'Director of the Master'; the Italian microsite page updated 03/12/2025 names 'Tutor: Prof.ssa Mara FERRERI'. Both are DIST academics on the pathway; the discrepancy is a maintenance artefact, but it means contact details should be verified before writing.

13) FEES AND SCHOLARSHIPS FOR 2026/27 NOT FULLY PUBLISHED. Only the 2025/26 range (EUR 156-2,800 per year, income-dependent) is confirmed; UNITO says the 2026-27 contribution information is on the University portal, which returns 403 to automated fetches. It is also undocumented how the contribution works for an interuniversity UNITO/Politecnico degree. The 'Talents 4 UniTO' call (40 two-year scholarships for international students first-enrolling in an English-taught open-access postgraduate degree - this course qualifies) is CLOSED for 2026/27 with the ranking already published; the programme brochure separately advertises 'merit-base or income-base full-stipend scholarships' without giving amounts, numbers or a call link.

14) ACCESS LIMITATIONS DURING RESEARCH. All *.unito.it hosts (www.geography.unito.it, www.geografia.unito.it, www.unito.it, en.unito.it) refused direct automated requests at network level (connection refused to 130.186.3.24:443, or HTTP 403), so every microsite page and the brochure PDF were retrieved through Internet Archive snapshots, and the UNITO catalogue entries only through search snippets. Everything sourced from apply.unito.it (course record, JSON feed and the five news pages) WAS fetched live on 1 September 2026 and is the most reliable layer of this record. polito.it was deliberately excluded per the research scope.

15) CONTACT POINTS FOR VERIFICATION. Prof. Michele Lancione, michele.lancione@unito.it (Director of the Master); Ms Rossana Petean, rossana.petean@unito.it (student office); francesco.chiodelli@unito.it (English microsite contact); Prof. Giandomenico Fubelli, giandomenico.fubelli@unito.it and Prof. Piero Bonavero, piero.bonavero@unito.it / Prof.ssa Paola Pressenda, paola.pressenda@unito.it (interview syllabus queries, physical and human geography respectively); internationalstudents@unito.it (International Students Office).
